evidence.note: CONFIRMED: before the fix, a cycle where the victim holds two leases in the waiter's way made autoorder._candidates order only ('T2','T1') and propose return one edge, and health._cycle_locks returned LOCKED only for the waiter item, missing the second dropped lease. Cheap test = AO.propose with victim blockers ['T2','T4'] -> edges [('T2','T1')] (bug) then [('T2','T1'),('T4','T1')] (fixed); H.inspect over the alpha/beta cycle -> ['alpha','beta','check','docs'] locked items.

Followed r-gemini-key-load (will export GEMINI_API_KEY before review), touched only the two reader files in the fix globs plus the two regression test files, wrote the regression test first, kept deterministic ordering.

autoorder._victim_items() + _candidates() order every dropped lease; propose() adds an edge per dropped item instead of stopping after the first; health._link_locks() + _cycle_locks() emit a LOCKED row for every blocking lease. Regression tests in tests/test_conflict_autoorder.py and tests/test_health_watch.py.

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture puts the two asserted entries in `"blockers"` while the link still has only a single `"item": "check"` and no `"items"` list. The health half of B-autoorder-first-drop-only is that `_cycle_locks` reads only `link.item`, so a second *wait* of the same agent is missing; the intent says the new `Link.items` field carries those waits. This test never supplies a second wait, so a broken `_link_locks` that continues to ignore `Link.items` and merely iterates `blockers` would make this test pass, leaving the stated second-wait bug untested. The test exercises the auto-order victim-drop scenario, not the health second-wait scenario it claims to cover.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_health_watch.py::test_every_lease_the_victim_drops_gets_a_locked_row

chunk_findings.detail: The “already ordered” branch still breaks after examining only the first victim candidate. If `_victim_items(cycle)` returns two dropped leases such as `["lease-A1", "lease-A2"]` and the existing needs graph already contains `lease-A1 -> lease-B` (precisely the state left by the old first-drop-only autoorder), the first candidate `("lease-A1", "lease-B")` hits `earlier in reach(later)`, sets `resolved = True`, and breaks. The loop never examines `("lease-A2", "lease-B")`, so no edge is added for the second dropped lease. That leaves the second lease able to take the files back, meaning the fix does not repair existing partially-ordered autoorder data.

chunk_findings.detail: After the victim pairs are handled the loop does not stop: `break` runs only when the pair just handled has `later not in victims`, so execution always falls through into the old fallback pairs and, unless that pair would close a cycle, appends an extra edge. Given a 3-cycle with `victim_item` Ta and links (Tb blocked by Ta), (Tc blocked by Tb), (Ta blocked by Tc) and no prior needs, candidates are (Ta, Tb), (Tb, Ta), (Tc, Tb). It adds (Ta, Tb), skips (Tb, Ta) as a cycle, then adds (Tc, Tb). Previously only (Ta, Tb) was returned; (Tc, Tb) forces Tc to wait for Tb after the deadlock is already broken. The same flag also treats the cycle as resolved from the first already-ordered victim pair and then drops later failure notes: with T2 already needing T1 and T1 already needing T4, victims {T2, T4} produce no edge and no note while T4 can still take the files back.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression meant to close B-autoorder-first-drop-only never builds the case the bug describes. The stated miss is a second wait of the same agent (Link.items) and victim drops (Cycle.drops); this fixture has one link per agent, no `items`, and no `drops`, and only stuffs a second lease into `blockers` on P’s single link (`item` is `"check"`, `blocker` is `"alpha"`, `blockers` is `["alpha","beta"]`). `H.inspect` is then required to surface finding items `"alpha"` and `"beta"`. A reader that still uses link `item` only, or that correctly walks `Link.items` / `Cycle.drops` and ignores `blockers`, is not what this assertion checks, so the test can stay red after the real fix or go green on a `blockers`-only special case and still leave the second wait without a LOCKED row.

chunk_findings.detail: A successful fallback edge is not recorded, so the failure note still fires. `added` is only incremented in the victim-drop loop, and the fallback `_ADDED` branch just `break`s without setting `already`. Given a cycle with no `victim_item`, agents `("Tb", "Ta")`, and one link `item="Tb"` blocked by `"Ta"` (both eligible, empty `needs`), `_take` appends `Edge("Tb", "Ta", ...)` and returns `_ADDED`, then `added == 0 and not already` is still true, so the return is `(edges=[that edge], notes=["no edge for Tb -> Ta: ..."])`. The same false note is emitted when every victim-drop pair is `_SKIP` and the fallback pair is the one that actually orders the cycle.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/autoorder.py:165

chunk_findings.detail: Fallback still runs after a victim drop that is already ordered. The guard is `if added == 0`, and `_ALREADY` never increments `added`. Given victim item `Ta`, links `(Tb blocked by Ta)`, `(Tc blocked by Tb)`, `(Ta blocked by Tc)`, and `needs` already containing `Ta -> Tb`, the drop pair returns `_ALREADY` (`added` stays 0, `already` becomes true) and the fallback loop still appends `Edge("Tc", "Tb", ...)`. That is an extra ordering the drop did not need; the comment says the fallback is only for when no drop could be ordered.
